elements.element: Transition assistance provided on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Assistance available for up to 6 months
Customer Data returned within 30 days of expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for download all Customer Data" — the deadline runs from a later request, not from expiry or termination

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" — machine-readable is present but the required "standard" format qualifier is replaced with "commonly used"

elements.element: Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: "(c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems"

elements.element: At least 90 days of transition assistance
elements.evidence: "transition assistance for up to six (6) months"
"within thirty (30) days of Customer's request" — export duty is conditioned on and measured from a Customer request rather than being a fixed 30-day post-termination obligation

offending_extra_words: subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements
reasons: Preferred level fails: the 30-day Customer Data return deadline runs from "Customer's request" rather than from expiry or termination, so a delayed or overlooked request defers the mandatory return indefinitely.
Preferred level also fails on format: "commonly used, machine-readable format" substitutes a softer qualifier for the required standard machine-readable format.

Fallback is not independently satisfied either, because the 30-day export deadline is measured from a request instead of termination; a request condition must not swallow the mandatory post-termination data return.

Not minimal: the insertion adds a broad new carve-out ("subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements") and softeners ("reasonable", "at Customer's request") that were not needed to complete the preferred position.

Intent concern: triggering the new data-return, deletion and certification duties on expiry or termination of "any Order Form" can force deletion of Customer Data while other Order Forms and Services remain live, conflicting with clause 10.1's continuing rights in Customer Data.

Fix: change to "within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination", state "a standard machine-readable format", drop the backup/legal-retention carve-out or narrow it to legally required retention, and limit the trigger to expiry or termination of this Agreement.
